_meta.what: Political and economic levers for the page's Conditions panel. Each effect is a multiplier on visitors or residents' spending, or a change in business costs as a share of revenue, relative to the calibrated year (2025). 'measured' effects come from data; 'SEED' effects are stated assumptions.
_meta.closure_response: Two-year closure odds are multiplied by exp(gamma x profit squeeze), the squeeze being extra costs plus lost gross margin as a share of revenue. SEED gamma = 40 (a squeeze of 1% of revenue raises the odds by about half): yearly closures in the Employment Inventory roughly doubled from 2016-2019 to 2022-2025 while the prime rate rose about 2.3 points (debt costs about 0.5% of revenue), but that period also had pandemic debts and CEBA repayments, so only part of the doubling is credited to rates.

today.as_of: October 2026 (Bank of Canada; Ontario minimum wage from October 2025)

interest_rate.sources: Debt 20% of revenue: SEED (prep/nfprep/survival.py DEBT_RATIO). Residents' spending -0.7% per point of prime rate: SEED, in the range of Bank of Canada estimates of how rate changes pass to consumption over a year or two.

tariffs.sources: US overnight visitors through Niagara fell to 0.882 of 2024 in 2025 (Statistics Canada 24-10-0053, measured); 'none' undoes that drop, 'escalation' repeats it (SEED). Canadians' trips to the US fell 30% in 2025 and they travelled at home; domestic visitors -5% if that unwinds, +3% if it deepens (SEED). Goods cost: counter-tariffs on US goods raise the cost of goods sold by about 2% in an escalation (SEED); removing them lowers it 1%.

exchange_rate.sources: US overnight visitors against the US dollar's price in Canadian dollars, 67 ordinary months 2017-2026: elasticity 0.84 (measured; correlation only 0.15, a weak link).

minimum_wage.sources: Share of a kind's wages that move with the minimum wage: SEED (prep/nfprep/survival.py). Wage costs from Statistics Canada industry benchmarks.
